transcript:
Header: 2025-06-03 09:00 PT | Duration: 55m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jenna Ortiz, Marcus Lee, Priya Nair - Redwood; Alex Morgan, Rita Chen, Samir Patel, Hannah Li, Leo Park - Sequoia Payments
Shared artifacts: renewal-draft-2025.pdf, sequoia-sample-traces.csv, redwood-security-pack-link (sent in chat)

00:00 Jenna Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for making time today. quick agenda — renewal, capacity uplift, add APAC, and sync on compliance. Alex you wanted to lead on expected load?
00:12 Alex Morgan: Yeah thanks Jenna. So we're expecting a +40% token volume in Q3 after the August campaign. current baseline is about 4.5b tokens/day, peak bursts to ~7b for short windows. we need a predictable plan not surprise throttles.
00:28 Marcus Lee: Got it. that's helpful. our usual pattern would be reserved capacity with burst overlay. for the numbers you said, we'd recommend increasing reserved pool to match 6.5b steady with 1.5b burst on demand. that keeps latency SLOs tight.
00:41 Rita Chen: can you outline the latency numbers? our SLA target is p95 < 180ms for short responses, and < 400ms for long form, otherwise product team freaks out.
00:55 Marcus Lee: on Hosted with current model profiles we see median generation token latencies around 40-60ms on those sequence lengths, p95 closer to 140-200ms depending on batch sizing. Dedicated lowers variance — p95 typically drops by ~30%. there is tradeoff with cost though.
01:14 Samir Patel: cost is real. what's the delta on reserved vs hosted? we need ballpark to go to finance today.
01:22 Jenna Ortiz: I'll share a line-item: reserved capacity commit for your tier + APAC region add-on adds roughly 22% to hosted-only spend but gives you predictable throughput and better p95. exacts in the quote i'll send after this call.
01:35 Hannah Li: Security — quick T: we need KMS integ, customer-managed keys, SAML SSO, and audit logs. also need to know if private deployment (VPC / on-prem) is required for payments data. any existing customers set this up?
01:52 Priya Nair: Hi Hannah — yes we've onboarded several fintechs. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and SAML. audit logs and per-token retention controls are available. note: Private does increase lead time for provisioning — typically 4-6 weeks for VPC + HSM integration.
02:12 Hannah Li: And SOC 2? we need evidence of recent report.
02:16 Jenna Ortiz: we are SOC 2 Type II and can share the attestation (redwood-security-pack-link). i'll push the latest certs after the meeting.
02:26 Leo Park: for rollout — we want a canary by region. add APAC first for read-only features then full write lanes. how hard is region pinning?
02:36 Marcus Lee: region pinning is policy-driven. we can route by region and service tier, with automatic fallback to a secondary region if capacity constrained. for APAC, we'll stand up an instance in tokyo region, and route traffic there. can do canary routing at 5-10% initially.
02:52 Alex Morgan: timeline? we need APAC live before end of July if possible.
02:56 Marcus Lee: feasible if we sign by mid-June. we need perf tests and capacity provisioning lead time 3-4 weeks for Dedicated pools in APAC. if going Hosted it can be faster but less isolated.
03:09 Samir Patel: about benchmarking — Marcus you mentioned a 24h run; what will you measure?
03:16 Marcus Lee: we'll run your sample traces, measure token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and KV cache hit-rate impact. we'll also check tail latencies during synthetic burst windows. expecting to deliver a report within 48 hours after run completes.
03:31 Jenna Ortiz: okay action item: Marcus will run the run and upload the results. I'll send the revised quote with a 12-month extension option, and an add-on for APAC with dedicated pool.
03:43 Alex Morgan: on contracts, can we get a month-to-month for burst above committed? we don't want to be locked into a huge commit for short promo spikes.
03:51 Jenna Ortiz: Yes, we'll include burst credits and an overage rate sheet. also include optional burst buffer purchase. finance usually likes a blended commitment that matches forecast but with clear overage terms.
04:03 Hannah Li: one technical caveat — our compliance team may require an on-prem pilot if residual risk stays. can you run a feasibility checklist?
04:12 Priya Nair: we have a Private feasibility checklist — i'll attach it. for on-prem we'll need hardware inventory and expected network topology. initial scoping call typically required.
04:24 Rita Chen: if we did Private, would we keep the same API surface? we don't want to rework integrations.
04:30 Marcus Lee: yes same API, same SDKs, same rollouts. the main differences are networking and key management. there can be slightly different latency characteristics depending on local infra.
04:42 Alex Morgan: competitor question — BigCloud AI offered a lower list price but no KMS customer-managed keys and unclear audit retention. that's part of our risk calculus.
04:53 Jenna Ortiz: understood. that's often where Redwood differentiates — production controls and observability. we'll include the observability addon pricing in the quote.
05:02 Leo Park: ok. what's the decision gate timeline?
05:05 Alex Morgan: goal is internal signoff by 6/20. procurement + legal will review T&Cs, security has to sign off on KMS / SOC2.
05:13 Jenna Ortiz: recap: Marcus runs bench (due 6/9). Jenna sends quote + PO template (due 6/5). Hannah to confirm security open questions (due 6/10). Alex confirms volume forecast (due 6/12).
05:28 Samir Patel: any follow-up meeting?
05:30 Jenna Ortiz: let's do a results review w/ the bench in ~1 week after Marcus uploads. I'll send calendar invites. thanks everyone.
05:38 Alex Morgan: thanks all.
05:40 [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels, some words (KV cache, KMS) transcribed as K-V cash / K-M-S in auto transcript. There were brief cross-talk moments around 02:30-02:40.
